name: html-nav-equivalent-variant-disclosure-toggle
description: A source page declares the same navigation twice: an inline desktop menu whose trailing overflow control is a labelless anchor with aria-expanded (href="#"), and a hidden mobile-panel counterpart whose equivalent overflow control is instead a native <details>/<summary> disclosure. The two menus carry identical real destination links, so the desktop nav's overlay must resolve to 'mobile' (Core renders the responsive overlay and enqueues the navigation/view Interactivity module) even though the two overflow-toggle representations differ. Before this fix, the desktop menu's overflow anchor was folded into the nav's link signature, so the two menus compared as non-equivalent and the desktop nav silently downgraded to overlayMenu='never' -- dropping the mobile hamburger behavior even though the source unambiguously declares a mobile counterpart.

source_reference.notes: Product-neutral fixture derived from a real-world regression: a page builder's responsive header renders the same overflow ('More') toggle as a bare anchor in one menu instance and as a <details>/<summary> disclosure in its mobile counterpart. Detection is structural (nav landmark identity by real link signature); no vendor-specific markup is referenced.

legacy_comparison.reason: This upstream primitive fixture has no downstream legacy comparison.
